Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-boost-polish-medium-0037", "row_sha256": "8bf92821f8bb6536a678eb5b3906773dd7ed3c5367752d9138a73a0a35773de2", "mode": "/polish", "language": "en", "context": {"profile": "Plain and direct."}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Rewrite awkward phrasing into readable prose for the supplied profile, or plain prose when none is supplied. Preserve intent and certainty. Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "can you tidy the wording on our family meal calendar for next week so everyone can tell what to cook and when? It is for me, my partner, and our two kids, and we are planning dinners at home from Monday through Friday. Keep Monday as pasta with peas and Tuesday as leftover vegetable soup; those meals are already agreed on, so please do not switch them around. For Wednesday, write baked potatoes with beans, and note that the salad is optional rather than part of the meal everyone has to make. Thursday depends on Maya's work schedule: if she gets home by 6 p.m., put the chicken-and-rice bowls on Thursday. If she does not get home by 6 p.m., move the bowls to Friday and list sandwiches for Thursday instead. Please make the two Thursday options easy to distinguish so nobody reads them as plans to serve both. Keep Friday's entry conditional too, since the bowls should appear there only if Maya is late; otherwise Friday should stay open, not be filled with another meal. Add a short note at the top that the calendar covers dinner only, and leave the weekend blank. Don't turn the wording into a shopping list or add ingredients we haven't named.", "output": "Please tidy the wording on our family meal calendar for next week so everyone can tell what to cook and when. The calendar is for me, my partner, and our two kids, and covers dinners at home from Monday through Friday. Keep Monday as pasta with peas and Tuesday as leftover vegetable soup; those meals are already agreed on, so please do not switch them. For Wednesday, list baked potatoes with beans and note that the salad is optional. Thursday depends on Maya's work schedule: if she gets home by 6 p.m., put the chicken-and-rice bowls on Thursday. If she does not get home by 6 p.m., move the bowls to Friday and list sandwiches for Thursday instead. Make the two Thursday options easy to distinguish so nobody reads them as plans to serve both. Keep Friday conditional as well: the bowls should appear there only if Maya is late. Otherwise, leave Friday open rather than adding another meal. Add a short note at the top that the calendar covers dinner only, and leave the weekend blank. Don't turn the wording into a shopping list or add ingredients we haven't named."}]
